title: Introduce Prefer-Schema-Version header and runtime shim for schema negotiation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds opt-in request header Prefer-Schema-Version and a runtime compatibility shim that serves legacy schema shapes for clients that request them. No forced rollout; default behavior unchanged. See migration notes for client authors.
description: Motivation: Recent schema changes for structured output and function/tool-calling (v3) introduced subtle breaking surface changes in streaming event shapes and the function_call payload (args now emitted as structured JSON chunks). This caused customer incidents where older SDKs and proxies dropped events or mis-parsed function args during streaming. This PR adds an explicit negotiation path so clients can opt into newer schema behavior while preserving legacy shapes for existing clients.

b7d4c12: runtime/compat: implement v3->v2 response mapper (streaming + final payload)
c3f9a00: runtime/tests: e2e tests for streaming shim (socket replay + backpressure)
d4e1185: docs: docs/compatibility: add header reference and migration guide
e9a5f33: ci: lint fixes and add compatibility unit test to presubmit
review_thread: Ethan: please add a metric that counts negotiated-v2 responses — we need visibility. Maya: added telemetry and a dashboard link in the docs commit. Sofia: overall approach looks good; two nits on naming (Prefer-Schema-Version vs X-Prefer-Schema) and a request to ensure header is ignored for websocket streaming upgrades. Maya: kept Prefer-Schema-Version per RFC semantics, wired the websocket negotiation to inspect initial upgrade headers and added tests. Devon: noticed a race where cached negotiation could return stale mapping after model reload; suggested TTL -> implemented a 30s TTL cache. Final: approvals from Ethan and Sofia, Devon approved after TTL fix.
ci_log: Presubmit: lint failed on first run (naming), fixed; unit tests initially 3 failing (streaming edge cases), added buffering and retry for partial JSON chunks; final pipeline green: all checks passed (unit/integration/e2e/compat-tests).
migration_notes: - Clients that want stable legacy behavior: send header Prefer-Schema-Version: v2 (or Prefer-Schema-Version: v2;q=1). The gateway will return legacy streaming delta shapes and legacy function_call args concatenated into choices[].message.content or function_call.arguments string as before. - Clients that opt into v3: send Prefer-Schema-Version: v3 or omit the header once v3 is default. - Deprecation: server will emit X-Redwood-Schema-Deprecation header when serving v2 shim; this is informational and will be removed in 2026-10-01. - SDKs: we added compat helpers in redwood-sdk-*; please upgrade to pick up negotiation helpers.
observability_changes: Added metric: redwood.compat.schema_negotiation.count{from=client,requested=v2,served=shim-v2} and histogram redwood.compat.shim_latency_ms. Added dashboard: Compat -> Schema Negotiation (docs link in PR).
performance_notes: Runtime shim adds a small CPU cost (~2-4% p50 on inference host) when active; shim path includes incremental translator and a bounded buffer for streaming re-assembly. We added a per-host cache keyed on (client-id, model, requested-version) to avoid repeated negotiation work (TTL 30s).

notes_for_support: SUP-4421: temporary workaround applied for customer acct-991: gateway was configured to force v2 shim for their router; recommended client upgrade and removed forced shim on 2026-01-18.
example_usage: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Prefer-Schema-Version: v2' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-encoder-3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Call the tool"}]}'\nThe response will contain streaming events with legacy 'delta' chunks and function_call.arguments as a single string in the final message.
notes: This PR is deliberately opt-in; default behavior for existing clients is unchanged. We avoided automatic rewrites to prevent surprising downstream proxies. The shim is limited to mapping shapes (no semantic changes to tokens or function selection).
